newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia may send troops for Zaire force.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia may send troops for Zaire force.

text.p: Australia might contribute troops to an international force in Zaire and defence chiefs had been ordered to prepare for a speedy deployment, Prime Minister John Howard said on Monday.
Howard said the situation remained too unclear to make a final commitment, but said his Liberal-National coalition government would continue to monitor developments closely.

"It is at this moment a situation which is too fluid and too unpredictable for Australia to make a definite decision as to what kind of commitment, if any, ought to be made, particularly when the circumstances of the force to which we might be commiting is itself a matter of very significant doubt," Howard told parliament.
The return home from Zaire of 500,000 Rwandan refugees has raised doubts among likely members of the multinational peace force for Zaire about the need for military intervention.
Australian officials had previously been cool on the idea of sending troops to Central Africa.
The United Nations refugee agency UNHCR estimated on Sunday that 400,000 Rwandan Hutus had already returned to Rwanda from eastern Zaire and 100,000 more were moving to the border.
About 10,000 soldiers are supposed to join a Canadian-led U.N. peacekeeping force, but the United States has not yet made a firm decision to join and the force's future remains unclear.
Howard said Canberra could provide more aid if needed and would consider joining a peacekeeping force.
"The disposition would of course be on the part of the government to look at the merits of any proposal that may be before us according to the circumstances as we assess them at the time," he said.
"The Australian defence forces have been instructed to take precautionary measures to shorten the deployment time if that were to become necessary."
